import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Create a comprehensive visualization with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# Calculate age and total spending
df['Age'] = 2024 - df['Year_Birth']
df['Total_Spending'] = (df['MntWines'] + df['MntFruits'] + df['MntMeatProducts'] + 
                         df['MntFishProducts'] + df['MntSweetProducts'] + df['MntGoldProds'])
df['Total_Purchases'] = (df['NumWebPurchases'] + df['NumCatalogPurchases'] + 
                          df['NumStorePurchases'] + df['NumDealsPurchases'])

# 1. Income Distribution by Education
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
education_order = df.groupby('Education')['Income'].median().sort_values().index
sns.boxplot(data=df, y='Education', x='Income', order=education_order, ax=ax1, palette='Set2')
ax1.set_title('Income Distribution by Education Level', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Income ($)', fontsize=10)
ax1.set_ylabel('Education', fontsize=10)

# 2. Age vs Total Spending (colored by Income)
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
scatter = ax2.scatter(df['Age'], df['Total_Spending'], c=df['Income'], 
                     alpha=0.6, s=30, cmap='viridis', edgecolors='k', linewidth=0.3)
ax2.set_title('Age vs Total Spending (colored by Income)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Age (years)', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_ylabel('Total Spending ($)', fontsize=10)
cbar = plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax2)
cbar.set_label('Income ($)', fontsize=9)

# 3. Product Category Spending Distribution
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
product_spending = {
    'Wines': df['MntWines'].sum(),
    'Meat': df['MntMeatProducts'].sum(),
    'Fish': df['MntFishProducts'].sum(),
    'Fruits': df['MntFruits'].sum(),
    'Sweets': df['MntSweetProducts'].sum(),
    'Gold': df['MntGoldProds'].sum()
}
colors = sns.color_palette('Set3', len(product_spending))
ax3.pie(product_spending.values(), labels=product_spending.keys(), autopct='%1.1f%%',
        startangle=90, colors=colors)
ax3.set_title('Product Category Spending Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 4. Marital Status Distribution
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
marital_counts = df['Marital_Status'].value_counts()
sns.barplot(x=marital_counts.index, y=marital_counts.values, ax=ax4, palette='muted')
ax4.set_title('Customer Distribution by Marital Status', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Marital Status', fontsize=10)
ax4.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=10)
ax4.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 5. Purchase Channel Comparison
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
purchase_channels = {
    'Web': df['NumWebPurchases'].sum(),
    'Catalog': df['NumCatalogPurchases'].sum(),
    'Store': df['NumStorePurchases'].sum(),
    'Deals': df['NumDealsPurchases'].sum()
}
bars = ax5.bar(purchase_channels.keys(), purchase_channels.values(), 
               color=['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4', '#45B7D1', '#FFA07A'], edgecolor='black', linewidth=1.2)
ax5.set_title('Total Purchases by Channel', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_xlabel('Channel', fontsize=10)
ax5.set_ylabel('Total Purchases', fontsize=10)

ax6_twin = ax6.twinx()
